# Rollout Plan: Migrating 40,000 Users to New Billing System

## Overview
Both the old and new billing systems will run in parallel throughout the migration, allowing for gradual cutover, dual-write reconciliation, and fast rollback of individual cohorts without affecting already-migrated users.

---

## Phase 1: Pilot (2% of users — ~800 users)
**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed full parity testing in staging (invoicing, tax calculation, payment processing, refunds) against a mirrored copy of production data, and a rollback procedure has been tested end-to-end at least once.

- Select internal/employee accounts and opted-in low-risk external users (e.g., monthly billing, no active disputes).
- Run dual-write mode: transactions processed on old system, shadow-processed on new system, outputs diffed daily.
- Manual review of every invoice generated for this cohort during the phase.
- Duration: minimum 2 weeks or 2 full billing cycles, whichever is longer.

## Phase 2: Expanded Rollout (25% of users — ~10,000 users)
**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 completes with invoice/charge discrepancy rate below 0.1%, zero critical payment failures, and support ticket volume for migrated users within 1.5x of baseline.

- Migrate a randomized, representative sample across plan types, geographies, and payment methods (credit card, ACH, invoice-based).
- Move from shadow-processing to live processing on the new system for this cohort; old system retained as fallback for the phase duration.
- Automated reconciliation job runs every 4 hours comparing charge amounts, billing dates, and tax line items between systems' logs.
- Duration: minimum 3 weeks.

## Phase 3: General Availability (73% of users — ~29,200 users, completing to 100%)
**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 completes with discrepancy rate below 0.05%, no unresolved Sev-1/Sev-2 incidents in the prior 14 days, and customer support and finance teams have signed off on new-system reporting accuracy.

- Migrate remaining users in weekly waves of ~15–20% of the total user base to preserve rollback granularity, prioritizing by contract renewal date (migrate accounts furthest from renewal first).
- Old billing system remains fully operational in read/fallback mode throughout this phase — it is **not** disabled, deprecated, or decommissioned during or immediately after the final migration batch. Decommissioning is a separate, subsequent phase gated on a minimum 60-day stability soak period post-100%-migration with zero critical billing incidents.

---

## Risks

RISK: Payment data or charge discrepancies between old and new systems cause customers to be over- or under-billed | Run automated reconciliation every 4 hours during Phases 2–3 with daily manual spot-checks; auto-freeze new charges for any account showing a mismatch pending finance review | Finance Systems Lead

RISK: New system cannot handle peak transaction volume during month-end billing runs | Load-test new system at 3x expected peak volume before Phase 2 entry; stagger migrated accounts' billing dates across the month during Phase 2 | Platform/Infra Lead

RISK: Customer support is unprepared for new-system-specific billing questions, leading to service degradation | Train support staff and publish internal runbooks before each phase; embed a support liaison in the migration team during Phases 1–2 | Customer Support Manager

RISK: Rollback of a migrated cohort back to the old system results in data loss or duplicate charges | Build and test an idempotent rollback script with a dry-run mode prior to Phase 1; require rollback rehearsal sign-off before Phase 2 entry | Engineering Lead, Billing Platform

RISK: Tax calculation differences between systems create compliance exposure in certain jurisdictions | Run parallel tax-calculation audits per jurisdiction during Phase 1 pilot; require tax/compliance sign-off before expanding to new geographies in Phase 2/3 | Compliance Officer

---

## Halt Criteria
The rollout will be immediately paused (no further users migrated to the new system) if any of the following occur:

- **Billing discrepancy rate exceeds 0.5%** of transactions processed on the new system within any rolling 24-hour window.
- Payment failure rate for migrated users exceeds 2x the baseline failure rate on the old system for more than 6 hours.
- Any single Sev-1 incident (e.g., duplicate charges, failed payment processing at scale) affecting more than 100 accounts.

A halt triggers an automatic freeze on new migrations, an incident review, and a go/no-go decision from Engineering and Finance leads before resuming.

---
